jess: FYI ran nsys on the failing job (batcher_v2 + kv-prefetch) — attaching timeline snippet. huge tail where memcpy dominates and kernels look serialized.
jess: trace: https://artifacts/internal/nsys/2167773333-epoch3.qdlist (trimmed)
amar: can you paste the waterfall text? quick look suggests cudaMemcpyAsync on stream 3 is blocking later kernels on stream 1/2
jess: pasted snippets below:
```
Time    Stream  Activity
0.001   s1      triton_fused_attn_fwd
0.0015  s3      cudaMemcpyAsync H2D (prefetch_kv)
0.002   s1      sgemm_kernel
0.004   s3      cudaMemcpyAsync H2D (prefetch_kv)
0.006   s1      triton_attn_bwd
... (repeat pattern)
```
ryan: interesting — looks like prefetch_kv is using a separate stream but we probably enqueue with cudaStreamDefault affinity due to the new kernel-selection path. that can serialize with host->device copies if pinned memory falls back.
sabrina: we also landed the batcher heuristic change in commit 9a3f7b4 which increases microbatch size when sequence_len < 128. might be increasing concurrent prefetches so memcpy backlog grows.
amar: could also be CPU-side: prefetch threads might get preempted causing delayed stream submission -> cudaDriver serializes and you see memcpy pile-up. any perfetto cpu sched slices?
jess: yes i ran perfetto + nsys. CPU shows bursts where the prefetch worker is runnable but delayed ~8-12ms due to other kernel-worker threads from the executor. snippet:
```
PID  TID  DURATION  STATE
2345  2345  0.0002s  running (worker)
2346  2346  0.011s   runnable (prefetch)
2345  2345  0.002s  running
```
ryan: that matches. If prefetch_submit gets delayed, cuda memcpy ops queue up on the stream and then execute back-to-back, which can block small kernels that expect overlap.
sabrina: what about pinned memory pool? if prefetch uses staging pinned buffer but the pool is exhausted it will fall back to pageable and trigger synchronous hostcopy under the hood. any hostcopy calls in the trace?
jess: nsys shows both "cudaMemcpyAsync" and some "memcpy" labelled kernels — likely the driver falling back. pool metrics: pool_size=64MB, peak_used=64MB in this run. so yes exhausted.
amar: hypothesis: batcher_v2 increased microbatch concurrency -> more prefetches -> pinned pool exhausted -> fallbacks -> big H2D slowdowns serialized -> visible memcpy blocks kernels.
ryan: also check kernel selection: after the kernel-choice refactor we prefer sgemm_banked kernel for short seqs which has larger workspace per-context, could exacerbate memory pressure.
sabrina: reproduce plan: run a controlled job with environment overrides: set BATCHER_MAX_INFLIGHT=8, BATCHER_V2=false, PREFETCH_PINNED_POOL=128MB, and capture nsys+perfetto. compare token/s and 95p p99 latency.
jess: i'm running that now on dev-gpu-12. command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=gpu,osrt,cuda --sample=none -o /tmp/run2167773333 nvidia-run -- ./run_inference --profile
perfetto --txt -o /tmp/perfetto.pb 
```
ryan: when you have traces, grep for "cudaMemcpyAsync" + stream id ordering and also dump cupti correlation to see host-side enqueue times vs device start times. that will show submission jitter.
perf-ci-bot: CI note: regression alert at 2026-03-15 18:02 UTC, perf delta: -18% throughput on batcher_v2 microbench (short seq).
amar: ok actionable items: 1) jess finish controlled run and upload traces; 2) ryan add lightweight probe in prefetch_submit to log thread wake latency and pinned pool allocation failures; 3) sabrina try increasing pinned pool default and add fallback metric; 4) if reproduces, revert batcher heuristic or gate behind feature flag.
jess: uploaded traces to /artifacts/nsys/2167773333/ (full + perfetto). also put a trimmed waterfall PNG in the ticket.
sabrina: small optimization idea: instead of immediately scheduling prefetch for all microbatches, stagger prefetches with backoff when pinned pool pressure high. that should reduce simultaneous H2D spikes.
amar: agree. also evaluate switching prefetches to stream with higher priority or use separate copy engine streams to avoid interfering with compute streams. check cudaMemcpyKind and stream flags.
ryan: final tip: check cuBLAS workspace allocation size for sgemm_banked — if that increased dramatically for short seqs, it might be allocated on host and cause page faults. enable CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG to limit workspace.
jess: thanks all — i'll run the controlled experiment and post results here. pending: first-pass mitigation is increasing pinned pool and gating batcher_v2 feature flag.
(emoji reactions: :eyes: :thumbsup:)
